message.content:
Yes – you can quickly see whether **VS Code** (`Code.exe`) is currently running from a normal Command Prompt window (or even from PowerShell).  
Just type:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe"
```

### What it does

* `tasklist` lists all processes that are alive at the moment.  
* `/FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe"` filters the list so only entries whose executable name matches *exactly* “Code.exe” are shown.

If VS Code is running you’ll get something similar to this:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== =================== ========= ============
Code.exe                      12345 Console                    1     150,000 K
```

(Your numbers will differ.)

If nothing shows up after the header lines, then there’s no instance of `Code.exe` running.

---

#### Quick sanity‑check alternatives

| Shell | One‑liner |
|-------|-----------|
| CMD   | `tasklist /fi "imagename eq Code.exe" | findstr /i Code.exe` |
| PowerShell | `Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` |

Both return an object/line when VS Code is active, otherwise nothing.

So yes—your command works perfectly fine for checking whether VS Code is running.
